## Procedure and coverage

Patched update file installed from the card with OK held, then used over repeated power-ons, sleeps and a reinstall; emulator runs covered good and bad files, OK held, and late sections or card.

- Core starts by itself on every full power-on, about 1.4 to 1.7 s after it; without OMKIT the camera works as stock.
- Holding OK at power-on skips core.
- Reinstalling a firmware from the card with OK held works from the patched firmware.
- A quick lever off-on is not a new start; light sleep keeps core running and the film look comes back; deep sleep boots anew and loads core.
- A fault in core gives one restart into a camera without OMKit until the next load; on every start that is a reboot loop, ended by holding OK or removing the card.

## Limits and assumptions

- One developers' camera; counts of starts and the date of each check are not published; not reproduced by the Atlas.
- Wi-Fi and USB start paths are not verified.
- Whether the hook also runs when the camera starts its updater is not known; the documented rule is to keep OMKIT off update cards.
- The emulator does not run the real hook site; there the same loader body is hooked elsewhere.
- tested_on is the first day of the reported use; the package hash is the result the docs name as installed since then.
